shouldFix.title: The join describes g18-input-corpus.v1 as naming initial states from live exactByteIntent; that corpus cites no exactByteIntent and names no state, and the description is the stated basis for closing OBL-G18-INPUT-CORPUS
shouldFix.measuredLimb1_exactByteIntent: basedOn.inputCorpus.role reads 'Named initial states from live exactByteIntent.' The string exactByteIntent occurs zero times in g18-input-corpus.v1. That corpus's own whatIsAuthored reads 'Three named initial states quoting live G18 v2 namedCorpusNotAuthored', its basedOn.g18v2.role reads 'namedCorpusNotAuthored is quoted', and its authorityClaim names the three namedCorpusNotAuthored classes. So the corpus states three times that it quotes a different field. G18 v2 does carry exactByteIntent at eight paths, three under namedCorpusClasses and five under retainedEvidence, so the claim is not impossible — the corpus simply did not draw from it.
shouldFix.measuredLimb2_noStateIsNamed: The corpus's per-state keys are exactly {id, memberVerbatim, fixtureBytes, assertsNamedNotAuthored} on all three entries. There is no stateNamed field and no source field. Each entry carries a slug, its class name in memberVerbatim, NOT-AUTHORED, and the same class name again in assertsNamedNotAuthored. The join nonetheless reasons 'g18-input-corpus.v1 names initial states' and leftoverDesignOpenStanding declares 'leftover-design of unnamed G18 initial states is stale as a naming claim after g18-input-corpus.v1'.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: OBL-G18-INPUT-CORPUS is recorded leftoverDesign false at rideStanding specified-not-leftover on the strength of that description. A later D-000 act reading this ledger would take the initial-state naming layer as discharged. On limb 1 the description is false whatever naming standard applies, which is why this is reportable independently of the standards question in the disclosure below.
shouldFix.howTheErrorLooksLikeItArose: The role string 'Named initial states from live exactByteIntent. fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED. This join consumes that naming. It does not close leftover-design of fixture implementations.' is byte-identical to the corresponding role in g16-leftover-join.v2, where it is true — g16-input-corpus.v2 carries twelve states each with stateNamed and each citing exactByteIntent. The phrasing appears to have been carried across to an artifact that does not support it.
shouldFix.notABlocker: Nothing is invented — no journal, no encoding, no row, no D9 code. The obligation the dispatch protects, OBL-G18-FX-AUTHORING, remains leftoverDesign true and alone in summary.leftoverDesign. The DR-107 ledger reconciles exactly, so this is not the inventory-shortfall shape that produced my one blocker in this family. It is the same class as CLAUDE-G04IC-V1-SF1: a citation asserting a source its target does not contain.
shouldFix.suggestedRepair: Either correct both claims to say the corpus quotes G18 v2 namedCorpusNotAuthored, and hold OBL-G18-INPUT-CORPUS at leftoverDesign true until a corpus that names states exists; or land a G18 input corpus in the shape of g16-input-corpus.v2 — stateNamed and source per entry — and re-measure the obligation against it.

standardsDisclosure.why: The second limb above turns on whether repeating a class name counts as naming an initial state, and my own lane has answered that question both ways within one hour. The coordinator needs this on the record; withholding it would make the finding look narrower than it is.
standardsDisclosure.theInconsistency: Per-state keys of exactly {id, memberVerbatim, fixtureBytes, assertsNamedNotAuthored} appear in four input corpora. I rejected three of them — g16-input-corpus.v1, g19-input-corpus.v1 and g22-input-corpus.v1 — for naming no state. I accepted the fourth, g18-input-corpus.v1, at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, reasoning in that verdict that 'the established shape for a NAMES-only input corpus' set a precedent and that 'the minimality is the discipline'. The G16 rejection and the G18 acceptance carry the same timestamp hour.
standardsDisclosure.whatIAmNotDoing: I am not re-opening g18-input-corpus.v1. Its verdict is frozen, it is not my subject, and a reviewer should not use a downstream review to reverse an upstream verdict by side effect. The finding above rests on limb 1, which is false under either standard.
standardsDisclosure.whatTheCoordinatorShouldDecide: Whether the NAMES-only shape discharges an initial-state naming obligation. If it does, three of my rejections were wrong and those corpora should be re-measured. If it does not, g18-input-corpus.v1's acceptance was wrong and this join's OBL-G18-INPUT-CORPUS closure has no basis at all rather than merely a misdescribed one. Either way the answer should be recorded once and applied to all four.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 SHOULD-FIX, 0 blockers. Twenty-eight attacks run; twenty-seven refuted, including every attack the prompt names. Custody holds: subject 189e7319 measured at start, again after the prompt repair, and at end; 0444, 15148 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified and matching their recorded pins; all thirteen recordedInputs files reproduce with basedOn cross-checked against them at zero disagreements. An instrument note first: the review-prompt file was blank in five fields when I first read it — subject path, digest, both write paths and HEAD. The dispatch supplied all five, the prompt was repaired mid-review, and the repaired version agrees with the dispatch throughout. The prompt is not the subject and this is not a finding against it. The finding is that the join misdescribes a pinned artifact, and the misdescription is the stated basis for closing an obligation. basedOn.inputCorpus.role reads 'Named initial states from live exactByteIntent.' The string exactByteIntent occurs zero times in g18-input-corpus.v1, and that corpus says three times in its own bytes — whatIsAuthored, its harness role, and its authorityClaim — that it quotes namedCorpusNotAuthored instead. G18 v2 does carry exactByteIntent at eight paths, so the claim is not impossible; the corpus simply did not draw from it. The role string is byte-identical to the corresponding role in g16-leftover-join.v2, where it is true, which is how the error looks to have arisen. Second limb: that corpus's per-state keys are exactly {id, memberVerbatim, fixtureBytes, assertsNamedNotAuthored} with no stateNamed and no source — a slug, the class name, NOT-AUTHORED, and the class name again — yet the join reasons that it 'names initial states' and moves OBL-G18-INPUT-CORPUS to leftoverDesign false with leftoverDesignOpenStanding declaring the unnamed-initial-states leftover stale. I must disclose that the second limb turns on a standard my own lane has applied both ways within one hour: I rejected g16-input-corpus.v1, g19-input-corpus.v1 and g22-input-corpus.v1 for exactly that key shape, and accepted g18-input-corpus.v1 with it. I have not reopened that frozen verdict — reversing an upstream by side effect in a downstream review is not a move a reviewer should make — and the finding rests on limb 1, which is false under either standard. The coordinator should settle once whether the NAMES-only shape discharges an initial-state naming obligation, and apply the answer to all four. Everything else in this join is correct and some of it is subtle. It keeps two register tokens apart without slipping once: DR-G18's own token is OPEN and DR-107's is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, both read independently from file 08, with the distinction stated in the registerRowNote, the basedOn role and doesNot, and corroborated by G18 v2's own leftoverNameNote. The owner cell is byte-identical to file 08's. The three corpus classes agree four ways. The DR-107 shortfall test is null — the live ledger's summary.leftoverDesign is exactly the two the join names. No journal is invented: fourteen journal mentions are two source quotations, one echo of file 08's own claim cell, and eleven refusals, and every structural probe for a format, schema, grammar, API, record declaration or fsync call returned zero. The file-04 parenthetical checks out at line 81. The successor diff is surgical — five obligations to six, one added, none removed, doesNot byte-identical at fifteen entries, summary.leftoverDesign unchanged — and all three limbs of my own predecessor-identity pattern are clean. Disclosure: all five Claude-lane verdicts this join pins are mine, including the one the finding concerns. What surfaced the finding was mechanical rather than intuitive — the join asserts properties of a pinned artifact, so I opened that artifact rather than accepting the description.
